study_identification_part.si4_title: Brain charts for the human lifespan

study_characteristics_part.sc1_study_objective: Aggregate multi-study MRI data to build lifespan brain reference charts and quantify individual differences via centile scores; demonstrate robustness and clinical utility across disorders.

rci9_quality_checking_detail.answer: EI available for 101,708 scans (82,023 subjects); excluded scans with |EI| > 2 MAD from study-specific median (~9–10% excluded); expert visual QC; robustness analyses showed highly correlated trajectories between EI-filtered and unfiltered data.
rci9_quality_checking_detail.reason: SI details the quantitative EI thresholding approach and its impact; multiple QC strategies described.
rci9_quality_checking_detail.supporting_text: "...EI was available (N=101,708 total scans on N=82,023 unique subjects)... exclude scans that had EI magnitude greater than 2 median absolute deviations... excluded approximately 9–10% of scans... model parameters were highly correlated..."

rci11_site_effect_handling_detail.answer: Study (site/study) treated as random effects on distribution parameters (e.g., Mu and Sigma) within GAMLSS; robustness evaluated via leave-one-study-out analyses; ComBat presented in comparison but not used for primary reference modeling.
rci11_site_effect_handling_detail.reason: SI explicitly motivates random-effects modeling for between-site heterogeneity and describes empirical evaluation compared to batch correction.
rci11_site_effect_handling_detail.supporting_text: "random-effects modelling strategy..."; "...GAMLSS modelling framework to correct for between-study differences... leave-one-study-out"; "comparison to ComBat"

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa7_association_analysis: Case–control and between-disorder comparisons of centile distributions across phenotypes with multiple-comparison control (FDR); stability/bias analyses via LOSO and bootstrap; sex-by-diagnosis models also reported.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa8_key_findings_brief: Brain charts yield robust lifespan centiles for common MRI phenotypes; centile deviations reveal disorder-specific patterns (e.g., markedly low GMV/high ventricles in AD; reduced centiles in SCZ), demonstrating standardized individual-level benchmarking across the lifespan.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa9_key_findings_detailed: Examples: For GMV, median centiles show AD substantially lower than CN (Female: CN 0.497 vs AD 0.152; Male: CN 0.491 vs AD 0.228). For Ventricular volume, AD shows markedly higher centiles (Female: CN 0.494 vs AD 0.826). SCZ also shows lower GMV centiles than CN (Female: 0.497 vs 0.228). These effects are consistent across multiple global phenotypes and supported by leave-one-study-out stability analyses.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa11_application_notes: Out-of-sample centile scoring with study-specific calibration; web resource (brainchart.io); variance modeling within GAMLSS improves handling of heteroscedasticity; centile scores show increased heritability vs raw phenotypes; CMD summarizes multivariate deviation.

caa10_key_limitations.answer: Potential sampling bias given known demographic/ascertainment biases in MRI studies; methodological heterogeneity across sites/scanners; current charts primarily for structural MRI phenotypes; fine-grained measures may be more sensitive to QC and harmonization limits.

general_note_part.gn1_general_notes: Datasets span prenatal to late-life and include numerous large cohorts (e.g., UKB, HCP, ABCD, ADNI, OASIS3, PING, PNC). Quality control combined automated EI filtering (~9–10% excluded at >2 MAD per study median) and expert visual checks. Between-study heterogeneity handled by study random effects within GAMLSS; LOSO analyses indicate robust trajectories. Independent validation included foetal ultrasound, head circumference references (WHO/INTERGROWTH), and post-mortem brain weight datasets. Full dataset list and acquisition/QC details are in Supplementary Reference database details and Table 1.1 CSV.
